Knowledge-base entry for 'Diaporthe':
────────────────────────────────────────
Parallel rows of black, flask-shaped specks or pycnidia on mature soybean stems occurring later in the season (R6 to R8 growth stages). Pycnidia may also develop on dry, poorly developed pods, but may be dispersed randomly rather than arranged linearly.. Parallel rows of black, flask-shaped pycnidia arranged linearly on stems; random dispersal on pods.
────────────────────────────────────────

Knowledge-base entry for 'Phomopsis':
────────────────────────────────────────
Infected seed are cracked, shriveled, dull, and may have a gray mold on them.. Seed infected by pod and stem blight may decompose after harvest and have low viability; seedlings grown from infected seeds may often be blighted.
────────────────────────────────────────

Knowledge-base entry for 'Phytophthora':
────────────────────────────────────────
Young plants show rapid yellowing and wilting with soft rot and collapse of the root. Mature plants exhibit general yellowing of lower leaves progressing upward, followed by wilting and death, with brown discolored roots and a dark chocolate-brown stem discoloration extending from below the soil line upward several nodes; leaves typically stay attached after plant death.. The best diagnostic symptom on susceptible varieties is a lower stem discoloration (dark chocolate-brown) that may extend several nodes up the stem. Root system shows lateral and branch roots almost completely discolored; tap roots with brown surface discoloration and tan to brown inner tissue discoloration. Leaves turn yellow, wilt, and typically stay attached after plant death.. stem canker, Pythium
────────────────────────────────────────

Knowledge-base entry for 'Bacterial_Blight':
────────────────────────────────────────
Infections begin as small, angular, water-soaked spots that turn yellow and then brown as the tissue dies. Lesions have dark reddish-brown centers surrounded by yellowish-green halos around water-soaked tissue; lesions may coalesce to form large, irregularly shaped lesions. Leaf veins may become affected creating necrotic areas resembling lightning on the leaf. Eventually lesions fall out leaving ragged foliage.. Presence of a yellowish-green halo around lesions; most common on young leaves in mid to upper canopy whereas brown spot is usually seen on older, lower leaves; lack of fungal structures in lesions.. Septoria brown spot, brown spot
────────────────────────────────────────

Knowledge-base entry for 'Green_stem_disorder':
────────────────────────────────────────
All or part of the soybean plant remains green while the rest of the plant or neighboring plants mature, most commonly seen in stems, leaves or pods; stems remain moist while pods and seeds have ripened.. Stems and occasionally leaves remain green and moist after pods and seeds have ripened and turned brown; excessive leaves on plant and green stems when neighboring plants are near harvest maturity.
────────────────────────────────────────

DISCRIMINATING: 'Diaporthe' vs 'Phomopsis'
Ruling feature : Location and arrangement of symptoms: Disease A shows linear rows of black pycnidia on stems, while Disease B affects seeds (cracked, shriveled, moldy)
Diaporthe: Parallel, linearly arranged rows of black, flask-shaped pycnidia (specks) on mature stems; pycnidia may also appear randomly on pods.
Phomopsis: Infected seeds appear cracked, shriveled, dull, and may carry gray mold; seeds decompose post-harvest and produce blighted seedlings.
Decision rule  : IF black flask-shaped pycnidia are arranged in parallel rows on the stem, THEN suspect Disease A (Diaporthe); IF the diagnostic sign is cracked, shriveled, dull seeds with gray mold rather than stem pycnidia, THEN suspect Disease B (Phomopsis).

DISCRIMINATING: 'Diaporthe' vs 'Phytophthora'
Ruling feature : Presence of discrete black flask-shaped pycnidia in parallel rows on stems (Disease A) vs. dark chocolate-brown internal stem discoloration extending upward from the soil line with no pycnidia (Disease B)
Diaporthe: Mature stems display parallel linear rows of black, flask-shaped pycnidia (visible surface structures); pycnidia may also appear randomly on pods. Symptoms occur late in the season (R6–R8).
Phytophthora: Dark chocolate-brown discoloration of the lower stem extending from below the soil line upward several nodes, accompanied by brown/discolored roots, general yellowing of lower leaves progressing upward, wilting, and leaves remaining attached after plant death.
Decision rule  : IF you see distinct black flask-shaped pycnidia arranged in parallel rows on the stem surface, THEN diagnose Diaporthe (Disease A); IF the stem shows a dark chocolate-brown internal/external discoloration beginning at or below the soil line with no surface pycnidia and leaves remaining attached after death, THEN diagnose Phytophthora (Disease B).
